answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making each identity climb a ladder whose rungs are countersigned work, not registrations. A newcomer starts on an isolated island with zero weight, must complete twenty attested tasks, and only then reaches the first vertex where its vote counts. Every rung costs a basalt-hard bond that is slashed on a failed audit, so a fleet of fakes must pay the full climb once per key. Clones therefore buy cost and delay, never influence.
